k_means_states.summary: k-means clusters of the standardised training bars; each cluster reads out its training up-rate and mean move.
k_means_states.implementationNote: Bridge: Lloyd's k-means on the training rows' standardised features (no labels); a bar takes its nearest centroid and P(up) = the state's Beta-smoothed training up-rate. Price: the cluster's shrunk mean scaled move. Differs from the spec: clusters carry no direction until the readout gives them one. Expect: P(up) near the base rate unless clusters separate persistent regimes.

initialization_count.label: Restarts
initialization_count.description: k-means++ restarts; the one with the lowest within-cluster sum of squares is kept.

readout_prior_strength.label: Readout prior strength
readout_prior_strength.description: How many pseudo-bars at the training base rate each state's up-rate (or mean move) is shrunk toward; a rarely visited state reads close to the base rate.

native.produces: A fixed number of centroids in feature space and, for every bar, the one centroid it sits nearest to.
native.targetVariable: Which centroid a feature row is closest to; the output says nothing about the direction or size of the coming price move.
native.objectiveNote: Lloyd's iterations lower the within-cluster sum of squared distances to the centroids and stop at a local minimum that depends on the starting centroids, which is why several initialisations are run.

metrics.why: The fit minimises squared distance from each training bar to its centroid, so the same distance on unseen bars, as a share of feature variance, is the algorithm's own objective measured out of sample.
metrics.baseline: Replacing every unseen bar with the training mean, which loses all of the feature variance.

metrics.why: More centroids always shrink the squared distance, so the silhouette adds the missing question of whether the centroids' cells are separated from each other or merely slice one cloud.
metrics.baseline: The same bars with their centroid labels shuffled, which gives a silhouette near zero.

metrics.why: Different starting centroids settle in different local minima, so a cell that does not hold the same bars after a reseed is an artefact of the start.
metrics.baseline: Chance agreement between two labelings, which the adjusted Rand index scores as zero.

metrics.why: A centroid's cell earns a name only if the bars inside it are followed by an up share different from the series as a whole.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series.

metrics.why: A centroid stranded on a few outlier bars wastes one of the requested clusters, and the size shares show it.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: A unit-root test describes an input series, and nearest-centroid assignment treats bars as unordered rows.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: The quantity belongs to fractional differencing of a price series, which is no part of moving centroids.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: The ratio belongs to principal components; for centroids the same information is one minus the held-out reconstruction error share, which is listed.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: Nearest-centroid assignment is fitted without labels and states no probability of an up move.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: A centroid label is not a position; a trading result appears only after the Model Cycle attaches an up-rate to each centroid.

notApplicable.name: Accuracy
notApplicable.why: There is no correct centroid to compare against, because the bars carry no group label before the algorithm runs.

asRun.standInNote: Lloyd's k-means is fitted on the standardised training rows without labels exactly as the specification describes; the up or down call is added by a readout that gives each centroid the Beta-smoothed up-rate of its training bars, so every as-run number measures centroids plus that readout and the within-cluster squared distance the fit minimised is not recorded.
asRun.probabilityNote: A bar takes its nearest centroid and the probability of up is that centroid's training up count pulled toward the fold's training up share by the readout_prior_strength dial; no curve is fitted on validation rows.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per bar, one value for the single fit; the training value scores the centroid up-rates on the training rows they were counted from and the validation value scores them on rows they never saw

meaningful.why: The probability of up is a smoothed count per centroid, and the bounded squared-error score tests whether each centroid's counted up-rate carries over to unseen bars.
It is what trading long when a bar's nearest centroid had a training up-rate of at least one half, and short otherwise, earned after costs under the engine's rule.
It relates the per-bar profit of the centroid up-rate calls to its variability; zero is an arithmetic marker and not a no-skill reference because a random caller pays costs.
It shows the deepest loss run while the position followed the side favoured by each bar's nearest centroid.
It compares winning and losing trades opened when price moved from a centroid favouring one side to a centroid favouring the other.
It counts winning trades of the centroid calls and must be read beside the trade count, because the call flips only when the nearest centroid changes side.
It tests the hard call from each centroid's up-rate against the actual direction, a call resting on up-rates that sit close to the training up share.
It shows whether the centroid calls recover both up bars and down bars or every centroid is called the training majority side.
It condenses the four outcome cells of the centroid calls into one number that stays at zero when all centroids are called the same side.
It tests whether centroids with a higher training up-rate are followed by more up bars, on a curve with one point per centroid set by cluster_count.
The readout is unweighted, so the gap between centroid up-rates and realised up shares is a fair check, though the up-rates crowd into very few bins.
It shows how far the centroid up-rates spread from the training up share, which is near nothing unless the cells separate lasting market conditions.
Each centroid carries one up-rate, so the level count is at most cluster_count and bounds what any ranking metric can show.
It shows whether the centroid up-rates fall on both sides of one half or the model called one direction on nearly every bar.
The forecast is the shrunk mean scaled move of the training bars at the nearest centroid, from a second fit of the same centroids, tested against forecasting no move.
It is the size of the miss of the centroid mean-move forecast in points, to be read beside the no-change forecast's error on the same bars.
It tests the sign of the centroid mean move, but shrunk means often round to zero ticks, so the denominator shown with it can be small.

Both curves are the logarithmic loss of the centroid up-rates, one on the training rows they were counted from and one on rows they never saw, so the difference is the readout's own overfit gap, which grows when the requested cluster count leaves some centroids with few training bars.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The up-rate is a smoothed count and not a likelihood fit, and how far it can move from the training up share is set by the readout_prior_strength dial, so the number mostly grades that dial.
With long_only off and no stop or target the engine is never flat once in a trade, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not the centroids.

caveats: The centroids are the best of initialization_count seeded starts on the fold's training rows, so a different seed can give different cells and different up-rates.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so any interval needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the Micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its own close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

gaussian_mixture_states.summary: A Gaussian mixture fitted by EM on the standardised training bars; a bar's soft membership weights each component's training up-rate.
gaussian_mixture_states.implementationNote: Bridge: a Gaussian mixture fitted by EM on standardised training rows (no labels); P(up) = sum over components of the bar's posterior responsibility times the component's responsibility-weighted Beta-smoothed training up-rate. Price: the same sum over mean scaled moves. Differs from the spec: direction comes only from the readout. Expect: soft, near-base-rate probabilities.

component_count.label: Components
component_count.description: How many Gaussian components the mixture has.

covariance_structure.label: Covariance structure
covariance_structure.description: Each component's covariance: full (any ellipsoid) or diagonal (axis-aligned).

covariance_regularization.label: Covariance regularization
covariance_regularization.description: Added to every covariance diagonal so a component never collapses onto a few bars.

readout_prior_strength.label: Readout prior strength
readout_prior_strength.description: How many pseudo-bars at the training base rate each state's up-rate (or mean move) is shrunk toward; a rarely visited state reads close to the base rate.

native.produces: A probability density over feature rows built from a weighted sum of Gaussian components, and for every bar the posterior share of responsibility each component takes for it.
native.targetVariable: How likely a feature row is under the fitted mixture and which component most plausibly generated it; the output says nothing about the direction of the coming price move.
native.objectiveNote: The mixture's likelihood is climbed by expectation-maximisation, alternating between sharing each bar among the components and refitting each component's weight, mean and covariance, and it reaches a local peak that depends on the starting point.

metrics.why: Expectation-maximisation raises the likelihood of the training bars, so the honest test is the mean log density the fitted bell-shaped components give to bars they never saw.
metrics.baseline: The same mixture reduced to a single Gaussian component fitted on the same training bars.

metrics.why: A full covariance per component has many free numbers, and a held-out log density far below the training one shows components that wrapped themselves around a few training bars.
Different starting points lead expectation-maximisation to different local peaks, so the component each bar is mostly assigned to must agree across seeds and adjacent folds.
metrics.baseline: Chance agreement between two labelings, which the adjusted Rand index scores as zero.

metrics.why: A component matters to a trader only if bars it takes most responsibility for are followed by an up share different from the series as a whole.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series.

metrics.why: The mixing weights show whether the requested component count is really used or whether one bell holds nearly every bar and the rest sit on a few outliers.
The mixture ignores the order of bars, so the run length of the leading component is a check of whether its components happen to be lasting market conditions or flicker bar to bar.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: A unit-root test describes an input series, and the mixture treats bars as exchangeable rows with no time order.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: The quantity belongs to fractional differencing of a price series, which is no part of fitting a mixture density.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette Score
notApplicable.why: The model is a density with soft overlapping elliptical components, which the silhouette's round hard groups misdescribe; held-out log-likelihood grades it instead.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: The ratio belongs to principal components; a mixture explains bars through likelihood, not through a share of variance.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction Residual
notApplicable.why: The mixture does not rebuild a bar from a code, and a distance to a component mean would ignore the covariances that define the model.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: Natively the mixture is a density of feature rows fitted without labels, so it states no probability of an up move to score.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: Responsibilities are not positions; a trading result appears only after the Model Cycle attaches an up-rate to each component.

asRun.standInNote: The mixture is fitted by expectation-maximisation on standardised training rows as the specification describes, without labels; the up or down call is added by a readout that gives each component a responsibility-weighted Beta-smoothed training up-rate, so every as-run number measures mixture plus that readout and the mixture's own likelihood is not recorded.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the sum over components of the bar's posterior responsibility times that component's responsibility-weighted training up-rate, each up-rate pulled toward the fold's training up share by the readout_prior_strength dial.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per bar, one value for the single fit; it grades the readout's blended probability of up, not the mixture's own likelihood, on the training rows the component up-rates were counted from for the training value and on rows they never saw for the validation value

meaningful.why: The probability of up blends smoothed component up-rates by responsibility, and the bounded squared-error score tests whether that blend holds on bars the mixture never saw.
It is what trading long when the responsibility-weighted blend of component up-rates reached one half, and short otherwise, earned after costs under the engine's rule.
It relates the per-bar profit of the blended up-rate calls to its variability; zero is an arithmetic marker and not a no-skill reference because a random caller pays costs.
It shows the deepest loss run while the position followed the side of the responsibility-weighted blend of component up-rates.
It compares winning and losing trades opened each time the blended component up-rate crossed one half, after costs.
It counts winning trades of the blended calls and must be read beside the trade count, because a blend hovering near one half can flip often and pay costs each time.
It tests the hard call from the blended component up-rate against the actual direction, a call that turns on small differences around the training up share.
It shows whether the blended calls recover both up bars and down bars or lean to the side every component favours.
It condenses the four outcome cells of the blended calls into one number that stays at zero when the blend never crosses one half.
Soft responsibilities make the blended probability continuous, so this is a genuine test of whether bars leaning toward high-up-rate components go up more often.
The readout is unweighted, so the gap between blended up-rates and realised up shares is a fair check, though the blend stays near the training up share and fills few bins.
It checks without bins whether the small departures of the blended up-rate from the training up share are the right size on unseen bars.
Averaging component up-rates by responsibility pulls every bar toward the middle, and this shows how little or how much spread survives.
It shows whether the blended up-rate fell on both sides of one half or the model called one direction on nearly every bar.
The forecast is the responsibility-weighted sum of each component's shrunk mean scaled move, from a second fit of the same mixture, tested against forecasting no move.
It is the size of the miss of the blended component mean-move forecast in points, to be read beside the no-change forecast's error on the same bars.
It tests the sign of the blended component mean move, but the blend often rounds to zero ticks, so the denominator shown with it can be small.

Both curves are the logarithmic loss of the blended component up-rates, one on the training rows they were counted from and one on rows they never saw, so the difference is the readout's own overfit gap; it is not the mixture's likelihood gap, which is not recorded.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The blended up-rate is built from smoothed counts and not from a likelihood fit to the labels, and its distance from the training up share is governed by the readout_prior_strength dial, so the number mostly grades that dial.
With long_only off and no stop or target the engine is never flat once in a trade, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not the mixture.

caveats: The mixture's own held-out log-likelihood, its native score, is not written to the record; only the readout's probability of up is scored.
Expectation-maximisation is started once per fit and may stop at its iteration limit, which the run log states, so the components are one local solution.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so any interval needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the Micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its own close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

hierarchical_clustering_states.summary: Agglomerative (bottom-up merges) or divisive (bisecting) clustering of spread training bars, cut at a cluster count; new bars vote by their nearest fitted bars.
hierarchical_clustering_states.implementationNote: Bridge: agglomerative linkage or divisive bisecting k-means on up to Maximum fit rows spread training rows, cut at Clusters; a new bar's cluster shares are a distance-weighted vote of its nearest fitted rows, and P(up) = those shares times each cluster's Beta-smoothed training up-rate. Differs from the spec: fitted on a subsample; new bars take their nearest clusters (the method has no predict). Expect: near-base-rate probabilities.

cluster_count.label: Clusters
cluster_count.description: Where the merge tree is cut: how many clusters remain.

hierarchy_direction.label: Direction
hierarchy_direction.description: Agglomerative merges bars bottom-up; divisive splits the data top-down (bisecting k-means).

linkage_rule.label: Linkage
linkage_rule.description: How agglomerative merging measures the distance between two clusters (Ward: least added variance).

maximum_fit_rows.label: Maximum fit rows
maximum_fit_rows.description: At most this many training rows, spread evenly over the training span, enter the clustering (its cost grows with the square of the row count).

neighbor_count.label: Extension neighbours
neighbor_count.description: A new bar's cluster is a distance-weighted vote of this many nearest fitted bars.

readout_prior_strength.label: Readout prior strength
readout_prior_strength.description: How many pseudo-bars at the training base rate each state's up-rate (or mean move) is shrunk toward; a rarely visited state reads close to the base rate.

native.produces: A tree of nested groups built by repeatedly merging the two closest groups or repeatedly splitting the largest, and a group label per bar once the tree is cut at a chosen number of groups.
native.targetVariable: Which branch of the merge tree a feature row falls under at the chosen cut; the output says nothing about the direction of the coming price move.
native.objectiveNote: Hierarchical clustering is greedy: each merge or split is the best single step under the linkage rule and is never revisited, so the tree optimises no global objective and the cut height is a choice.

metrics.why: With Ward, average or complete linkage the cut of the tree yields compact branches, and the silhouette asks whether each bar sits closer to its own branch than to the neighbouring one; for single linkage, which chains bars into long branches, it is not the right reading and the density-based index takes its place.
metrics.baseline: The same bars with their branch labels shuffled, which gives a silhouette near zero.

metrics.why: The agglomerative tree is a summary of all pairwise distances between bars, and the cophenetic correlation asks how faithfully the merge height at which two bars first join reproduces their original distance, whatever linkage rule built the tree.
metrics.baseline: The same tree with the merge heights shuffled among bar pairs, which gives a correlation near zero.

metrics.why: Ward linkage merges the branches whose union adds the least squared distance about the branch mean, and the divisive direction splits with bisecting k-means, so for those two variants the squared distance from an unseen bar to the mean of its branch, as a share of feature variance, is the quantity the tree was built to keep small; single, average and complete linkage branches have no such centre.
metrics.baseline: Replacing every unseen bar with the training mean, which loses all of the feature variance.

metrics.why: Single linkage joins bars through chains of near neighbours and so builds long thin branches that a compactness score misjudges, and this index grades such branches by how sparse they are inside against how empty the gap to the next branch is.
metrics.baseline: A single branch holding every bar, which has no gap between branches to measure.

metrics.why: An early greedy merge is never undone, so a few different bars can reshape the whole tree, and the cut must put the same bars together on a second fit.
metrics.baseline: Chance agreement between two labelings, which the adjusted Rand index scores as zero.

metrics.why: A branch of the tree is worth naming only if the bars under it are followed by an up share different from the series as a whole.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series.

metrics.why: Cutting a merge tree often leaves one large branch and several branches of a few stray bars, which the size shares expose at a glance.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: A unit-root test describes an input series, and the merge tree is built from pairwise distances between rows with no time model.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: The quantity belongs to fractional differencing of a price series, which plays no part in building a merge tree.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: The ratio belongs to principal components, and a merge tree has no components that explain variance.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: The tree is built from distances between unlabelled bars and states no probability of an up move.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: A branch label is not a position; a trading result appears only after the Model Cycle attaches an up-rate to each branch.

asRun.standInNote: The tree is built as the specification describes, by agglomerative linkage or by bisecting k-means for the divisive direction, but on an evenly spread subsample of training rows and cut at cluster_count; because the method cannot place a new bar, each bar's branch shares come from a distance-weighted vote of its nearest fitted rows, and the up or down call is added by a readout of each branch's Beta-smoothed training up-rate, so every as-run number measures tree plus vote plus readout.
asRun.probabilityNote: A bar's branch shares are a distance-weighted vote of its neighbor_count nearest fitted rows, and the probability of up is those shares times each branch's training up-rate pulled toward the fold's training up share by the readout_prior_strength dial.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per bar, one value for the single fit; the training value scores the voted branch up-rates on the training rows they were counted from and the validation value scores them on rows they never saw

meaningful.why: The probability of up mixes smoothed branch up-rates by a neighbour vote, and the bounded squared-error score tests whether that mix holds on bars outside the fitted subsample.
It is what trading long when the vote-weighted mix of branch up-rates reached one half, and short otherwise, earned after costs under the engine's rule.
It relates the per-bar profit of the branch up-rate calls to its variability; zero is an arithmetic marker and not a no-skill reference because a random caller pays costs.
It shows the deepest loss run while the position followed the side favoured by the branches a bar's nearest fitted rows belong to.
It compares winning and losing trades opened each time the vote-weighted branch up-rate crossed one half, after costs.
It counts winning trades of the branch calls and must be read beside the trade count, because the call flips only when a bar's neighbours change branch.
It tests the hard call from the vote-weighted branch up-rate against the actual direction, a call resting on up-rates that sit close to the training up share.
It shows whether the branch calls recover both up bars and down bars or lean to the side most branches favour.
It condenses the four outcome cells of the branch calls into one number that stays at zero when every branch is called the same side.
The neighbour vote makes the probability vary between bars near a branch boundary, so this tests whether bars voted toward high-up-rate branches go up more often.
The readout is unweighted, so the gap between voted branch up-rates and realised up shares is a fair check, though the values fill very few bins.
It shows how far the voted branch up-rates spread from the training up share after the prior and the vote have both pulled them inward.
It shows whether the branch up-rates fall on both sides of one half or the model called one direction on nearly every bar.
The forecast is the vote-weighted sum of each branch's shrunk mean scaled move, from a second fit of the same tree, tested against forecasting no move.
It is the size of the miss of the branch mean-move forecast in points, to be read beside the no-change forecast's error on the same bars.
It tests the sign of the branch mean move, but shrunk means often round to zero ticks, so the denominator shown with it can be small.

Both curves are the logarithmic loss of the voted branch up-rates, one on the training rows they were counted from and one on rows they never saw, so the difference is the readout's own overfit gap beyond what the neighbour vote already smooths.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The voted up-rate is built from smoothed counts and not from a likelihood fit, and its distance from the training up share is governed by the readout_prior_strength dial, so the number mostly grades that dial.
With long_only off and no stop or target the engine is never flat once in a trade, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not the tree.

caveats: The tree is built on at most maximum_fit_rows evenly spread training rows, and every other bar, training bars included, is placed by the neighbour vote and not by the tree itself.
The divisive direction is bisecting k-means, one particular splitting rule, and the linkage_rule dial applies to the agglomerative direction only.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so any interval needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the Micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its own close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

density_clustering_states.summary: Density clusters of the training bars on their leading principal components, plus a noise state for isolated bars.
density_clustering_states.implementationNote: Bridge: DBSCAN on the training rows' leading principal components, radius from the k-distance curve; a bar takes the cluster of its nearest core point within the radius, else the noise state, and P(up) = the state's Beta-smoothed training up-rate. Differs from the spec: density needs few dimensions, so it runs on principal components. Expect: few clusters plus noise; probabilities near the base rate.

principal_component_count.label: Principal components
principal_component_count.description: DBSCAN runs on this many leading principal components of the standardised training rows (whitened); 0 uses every standardised feature.

neighborhood_radius_quantile.label: Radius quantile
neighborhood_radius_quantile.description: The neighbourhood radius is this quantile of the training rows' distance to their k-th neighbour.

core_point_share.label: Core point share
core_point_share.description: A core point needs this share of the fitted rows inside its radius (at least twice the dimension).

maximum_fit_rows.label: Maximum fit rows
maximum_fit_rows.description: At most this many training rows, spread evenly over the training span, enter the density clustering (its cost grows with the square of the row count).

readout_prior_strength.label: Readout prior strength
readout_prior_strength.description: How many pseudo-bars at the training base rate each state's up-rate (or mean move) is shrunk toward; a rarely visited state reads close to the base rate.

native.produces: A group label for every bar that lies in a crowded region of feature space and a noise label for every bar that lies in an empty one, with the number and shape of the groups decided by the data.
native.targetVariable: Which density-connected group a feature row belongs to, or that it is noise; the output says nothing about the direction of the coming price move.
native.objectiveNote: The density method minimises and maximises nothing: groups are defined by density reachability, and a single deterministic sweep grows a group outward from every core point through neighbours inside the radius, so no loss value exists.

metrics.why: Groups grown by chaining core points can be long and curved, so they are judged by how thin the crowd is inside a group against how empty the gap between groups is, reported with the noise share.
metrics.baseline: A single group holding every bar, which has no gap between groups to measure.

metrics.why: A small change in the radius can merge two crowds or dissolve one into noise, so the same bars must land together in the next fit before a crowd is treated as real.
metrics.baseline: Chance agreement between two labelings, which the adjusted Rand index scores as zero.

metrics.why: The trading question is whether bars inside a crowd, or bars thrown out as noise, are followed by a different up share than the series as a whole.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series.

metrics.why: The radius and core-point count decide how many bars are called noise, and a fit that calls nearly everything noise or nearly everything one crowd has found no structure.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: A unit-root test describes an input series, and the density sweep counts neighbours of feature rows without modelling time.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: The quantity belongs to fractional differencing of a price series, a step this neighbour-counting method does not contain.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette Score
notApplicable.why: It is valid for compact groups only, and density-connected crowds of arbitrary shape with a noise label are graded by the density-based validation index instead.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: The method has no components and no centre per group, so no share of variance is explained by anything it outputs.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction Residual
notApplicable.why: A density-connected crowd has no representative point to rebuild a bar from, so there is no residual.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: The method assigns a crowd or noise label without ever seeing an outcome, so natively no probability exists to score.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: A crowd label is not a position; a trading result appears only after the Model Cycle attaches an up-rate to each crowd and to noise.

asRun.standInNote: The density sweep runs as the specification describes but on the leading principal components of an evenly spread subsample of training rows, with the radius read from the training k-distance curve; the up or down call is added by a readout that gives each crowd and the noise state the Beta-smoothed up-rate of its training bars, so every as-run number measures crowds plus that readout and none measures the clustering alone.
asRun.probabilityNote: A bar takes the crowd of its nearest core point when it lies inside the radius and the noise state otherwise, and the probability of up is that state's training up count pulled toward the fold's training up share by the readout_prior_strength dial.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per bar, one value for the single fit; the training value scores the crowd and noise up-rates on the training rows they were counted from and the validation value scores them on rows they never saw

meaningful.why: The probability of up is a smoothed count per crowd and for noise, and the bounded squared-error score tests whether those counted up-rates hold on unseen bars.
It is what trading long when a bar's crowd, or the noise state, had a training up-rate of at least one half, and short otherwise, earned after costs under the engine's rule.
It relates the per-bar profit of the crowd up-rate calls to its variability; zero is an arithmetic marker and not a no-skill reference because a random caller pays costs.
It shows the deepest loss run while the position followed the side favoured by the crowd or noise state of each bar.
It compares winning and losing trades opened when a bar moved between states whose up-rates sit on opposite sides of one half.
It counts winning trades of the crowd calls and must be read beside the trade count, because with few states the call flips rarely.
It tests the hard call from each state's up-rate against the actual direction, and with few crowds it can collapse to calling the training majority side.
It shows whether the crowd and noise calls recover both up bars and down bars or sit on one side for every state.
It condenses the four outcome cells of the crowd calls into one number that stays at zero when every state is called the same side.
It tests whether states with a higher training up-rate are followed by more up bars, but a few crowds plus noise give a curve of only a few points.
The readout is unweighted, so the gap between state up-rates and realised up shares is a fair check, though the few up-rates occupy very few bins.
It shows how far the crowd and noise up-rates spread from the training up share, which is the whole of what this model can say.
Each crowd and the noise state carry one up-rate, so the level count equals the states visited and bounds every ranking metric.
It shows whether any state's up-rate fell below one half or the model called up on every bar of the test span.
The forecast is the shrunk mean scaled move of the training bars in the bar's crowd or noise state, from a second fit of the same sweep, tested against forecasting no move.
It is the size of the miss of the state mean-move forecast in points, to be read beside the no-change forecast's error on the same bars.

With long_only off and no stop or target the engine is never flat once in a trade, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not the crowds.

caveats: Density is measured on the leading principal components set by principal_component_count, not on the full feature row, so the crowds are crowds along those axes only.

mean_shift_states.summary: Modes of the training bars' kernel density on their leading principal components; each mode reads out its training up-rate.
mean_shift_states.implementationNote: Bridge: mean shift finds the density modes of spread training rows on their leading principal components; a bar takes its nearest mode (modes under Minimum state share are merged into one state), and P(up) = the state's Beta-smoothed training up-rate. Differs from the spec: the mode count is capped by the merge. Expect: a handful of modes; probabilities near the base rate.

principal_component_count.label: Principal components
principal_component_count.description: Mean shift runs on this many leading principal components of the standardised training rows (whitened); 0 uses every standardised feature.

bandwidth_quantile.label: Bandwidth quantile
bandwidth_quantile.description: The kernel bandwidth is this quantile of the fitted rows' pairwise distances.

minimum_state_share.label: Minimum state share
minimum_state_share.description: A mode holding less than this share of the fitted rows is merged into one 'other' state.

maximum_fit_rows.label: Maximum fit rows
maximum_fit_rows.description: At most this many training rows, spread evenly over the training span, enter mean shift (its cost grows with the square of the row count).

readout_prior_strength.label: Readout prior strength
readout_prior_strength.description: How many pseudo-bars at the training base rate each state's up-rate (or mean move) is shrunk toward; a rarely visited state reads close to the base rate.

native.produces: A group label for every bar, given by the density peak (mode) that the bar's feature row climbs to when it is repeatedly moved to the kernel-weighted average of its neighbours, together with the list of modes; the number of groups is found, not chosen.
native.targetVariable: The feature row of a bar: which peak of the estimated density of feature rows that bar belongs to, with no statement about the direction of the next move.
native.objectiveNote: Mean shift's version climbs the kernel density estimate of the feature rows until each row reaches a local peak, so the bandwidth of the kernel is the only dial and it decides how many groups appear.

metrics.why: Mean shift defines a group as a hill of the kernel density, so the fair test is whether the rows around each mode are densely packed while the valleys between modes are sparse, which this index measures without assuming the hills are round.
metrics.baseline: The same index for the same rows with every row placed in a single group, which is what an over-wide bandwidth produces.

metrics.why: A small change of the kernel bandwidth or of the rows the density is estimated on can split or fuse a mode, so two fits of mean shift on shared bars must agree on which bars travel together before any mode is given a name.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the value two unrelated groupings of the same bars reach by chance.

metrics.why: The modes are found from feature rows alone, so the only evidence that a density peak is a market condition worth knowing is that the bars climbing to it are followed by a different up share than the series as a whole.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series.

metrics.why: Because the bandwidth sets the number of modes, a wide kernel sends nearly every bar to one peak and a narrow one scatters bars over many tiny peaks, and the share of bars per mode shows which of the two happened.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: A unit-root test describes a single input series before any model is fitted and says nothing about the density peaks that mean shift finds.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: This belongs to fractional differencing of an input series; mean shift reads each feature row on its own and keeps no memory to retain.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette Score
notApplicable.why: The silhouette assumes compact round groups, and a mean shift mode can be an elongated density ridge, so the density-based validation index replaces it for this model.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: Mean shift does not project the rows onto axes, so there is no retained variance to report; that figure belongs to principal component analysis.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction Residual
notApplicable.why: Mean shift never rebuilds a row from its mode and does not minimise the distance to the mode, so a rebuild error is not a score of its grouping.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: Mean shift states no probability of anything; a probability of up exists only after the Model Cycle attaches a training up-rate to each mode.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: A grouping of feature rows by density peak never takes a position, so there is no return stream of its own to divide by its swing.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter runs mean shift on the leading principal components of an evenly spread subsample of the standardised training rows, merges every mode that holds less than the minimum state share into one leftover state, and assigns a bar to its nearest mode instead of iterating the shift for that bar; the direction call is then read from each state's Beta-smoothed training up-rate, so every as-run number measures the density modes plus that counted readout and none of them measures the quality of the modes themselves.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up for a bar is the Beta-smoothed share of training bars in the same mean shift state that were followed by an up move, pulled toward the training up share by the readout prior strength dial, with no curve fitted on validation rows.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per bar, one value for the single fit

meaningful.why: Each mode's up-rate is a counted frequency, and the bounded squared-error score tests whether the up-rates the modes had in training are still the right odds on test bars without being blown up by a small state whose rate sits near an extreme.

The readout is an unweighted training frequency per mode, so comparing the stated up-rate with the up share actually observed on test bars is the direct test of whether a mode keeps its character out of sample.

It asks whether modes with a higher training up-rate are followed by more up bars on the test span, but with only a handful of modes the probability takes a handful of levels and the curve has that many points.
A bar takes exactly one mode, so the number of distinct probabilities equals the number of occupied states, and that count tells how coarse every ranking and calibration figure for this run is.
When the modes differ little in what followed them, or the prior strength dial is high, every state reads close to the training up share and the spread of the probability of up collapses toward zero.
With the readout prior strength dial at zero a small mode whose training bars all went one way reads exactly zero or one, and this count shows whether any test bar received such a rate.
The hit rate of calling up whenever a bar's mode had a training up-rate of at least one half, read against the fold's training majority class because modes near the base rate all make the same call.
It shows whether some modes are called up and others down, or whether every mode sits on the same side of one half so that the model calls a single direction on every bar.
One symmetric number for the hard calls of the mode readout that stays at zero when all modes land on the same side of one half.

What trading the mode's side of one half earned after costs under the engine's rule, read beside buy and hold on the same folds because a position changes only when a bar moves to a mode on the other side.
Net profit of the mode readout's calls per unit of bar-to-bar swing under the engine's rule, moved only by which side of one half each mode's up-rate fell on.
The deepest hole dug by holding the side each mode points to under the engine's always-in-the-market rule, a description of the traded path and not of the density modes.
Winning dollars over losing dollars of the trades closed when bars crossed between an up mode and a down mode, read with the trade count because few modes can mean few flips.
The share of closed trades from the mode readout that ended positive after costs, describing the engine's exit rule applied to these calls.
A second fit reads each mode's shrunk mean training move as the forecast, and this tests whether quoting the mode's average move beats forecasting no change on the same resolved bars.
The typical miss in points of quoting a mode's average training move, read beside the no-change forecast's miss because mode averages are small next to a single bar's move.
How often the sign of a mode's average move matched the realised move, counted only where the tick-rounded forecast is not zero, which for small mode averages can leave few bars.

The bandwidth quantile and the readout prior strength are searched on the engine's trading objective over inner training blocks, so this is an optimistic selection score to read beside the test value.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The up-rate is a counted frequency whose distance from the base rate is set by the prior strength dial and which can reach zero or one when that dial is zero, so the logarithmic loss grades the dial more than the modes; the Brier score is the proper score here.
The readout counts training bars without class weights, so its rates track the training up share and a class-balanced score would grade them against a prior they were never fitted toward.
With the default dials the engine is always long or short once the first call is made, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not anything the modes or the readout produced.

caveats: Mean shift runs on the leading principal components of the standardised training rows, and with the default of a single component the modes are peaks along one axis of the feature cloud.
The density is estimated on an evenly spread subsample of the training rows capped by the maximum fit rows dial, and a new bar joins its nearest mode without running the shift iteration.
Modes below the minimum state share are merged into one leftover state, so the number of states is smaller than the number of density peaks mean shift found.

The fit report holds one training value and one validation value, both the logarithmic loss of the readout's probability of up in nats per bar, not a score of the density modes, and the fit is reported as epoch one of one.
The price forecast comes from a second fit of the same adapter that reads each state's shrunk mean move, so its sign can disagree with the traded call read from the state's up-rate.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so intervals need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance, never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

affinity_propagation_states.summary: Exemplar bars chosen by message passing over the training bars' similarities; a bar reads out its nearest exemplar's up-rate.
affinity_propagation_states.implementationNote: Bridge: affinity propagation (responsibility and availability messages over negative squared distances) on up to Maximum fit rows spread training rows; a bar takes its nearest exemplar, and P(up) = the state's Beta-smoothed training up-rate. Differs from the spec: fitted on a subsample (quadratic in rows); new bars take their nearest exemplar. Expect: many small states; probabilities near the base rate.

preference_percentile.label: Preference percentile
preference_percentile.description: Each bar's self-preference is this percentile of the similarities: lower gives fewer exemplars.

damping.label: Damping
damping.description: How much of the previous message each update keeps (steadies convergence).

maximum_fit_rows.label: Maximum fit rows
maximum_fit_rows.description: At most this many training rows, spread evenly over the training span, enter affinity propagation (its cost grows with the square of the row count).

readout_prior_strength.label: Readout prior strength
readout_prior_strength.description: How many pseudo-bars at the training base rate each state's up-rate (or mean move) is shrunk toward; a rarely visited state reads close to the base rate.

native.produces: A set of exemplar bars chosen by message passing and, for every bar, the exemplar it belongs to, with the number of groups decided by the data and the preference setting rather than typed in.
native.targetVariable: Which exemplar bar each feature row is assigned to; the output says nothing about the direction or size of the coming price move.
native.objectiveNote: Affinity propagation maximises the net similarity, the summed similarity of every bar to its exemplar plus the preference of each bar that became an exemplar, by passing responsibility and availability messages rather than by descending a loss.

metrics.why: Each group is the set of bars sitting closest to one exemplar, so the groups are compact by design and the silhouette asks whether a bar really sits nearer its own exemplar's group than the next one.
metrics.baseline: The same bars with their exemplar assignments shuffled, which gives a silhouette near zero.

metrics.why: An exemplar stands in for every bar assigned to it, so the squared distance from an unseen bar to its nearest exemplar, as a share of feature variance, shows how much detail the exemplar set throws away.
metrics.baseline: Replacing every unseen bar with the training mean, which loses all of the feature variance.

metrics.why: The exemplar count swings with the preference and damping settings, so two fits on overlapping bars must put the same bars together before any exemplar can be named as a market condition.
metrics.baseline: Chance agreement between two labelings, which the adjusted Rand index scores as zero.

metrics.why: An exemplar group is only useful to a trader if the bars following its members go up more or less often than the series as a whole, which this checks per exemplar with a block bootstrap interval.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series.

metrics.why: Message passing often returns many small exemplar groups, and a group holding a handful of bars has an outcome record too thin to read.
The responsibility and availability messages can oscillate instead of settling, and exemplars read from unsettled messages are not the algorithm's answer.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: A unit-root test describes an input series, and affinity propagation compares feature rows pairwise without modelling any series through time.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: The quantity belongs to fractional differencing of a price series, and no differencing step exists in exemplar selection.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: The ratio belongs to principal components; for an exemplar set the same information is carried by the held-out reconstruction error share.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: Affinity propagation never sees a label and states no probability, so natively there is nothing for a probability score to grade.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: An exemplar assignment is not a position; a trading result appears only after the Model Cycle attaches an up-rate to each exemplar.

notApplicable.name: Accuracy
notApplicable.why: There is no correct exemplar to compare against, because the bars carry no group label before the algorithm runs.

asRun.standInNote: The exemplars are found as the specification describes, but on an evenly spread subsample of the training rows because the message passing is quadratic in rows; the up or down call is added by a readout that gives each exemplar the Beta-smoothed up-rate of the training bars nearest to it, so every as-run number measures exemplars plus that readout and none measures the clustering alone.
asRun.probabilityNote: A bar takes its nearest exemplar and the probability of up is that exemplar's training up count pulled toward the fold's training up share by the readout_prior_strength dial; no curve is fitted on validation rows.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per bar, one value for the single fit; the training value scores the exemplar up-rates on the training rows they were counted from and the validation value scores them on rows they never saw

meaningful.why: The probability of up is a smoothed count per exemplar, and the bounded squared-error score tests whether those counted up-rates carry over to bars the exemplars never saw.
It is what trading long when a bar's nearest exemplar had a training up-rate of at least one half, and short otherwise, earned after costs under the engine's rule.
It relates the per-bar profit of the exemplar up-rate calls to its variability; zero is an arithmetic marker and not a no-skill reference because a random caller pays costs.
It shows the deepest loss run while the position followed the side favoured by each bar's nearest exemplar.
It compares winning and losing trades opened when the nearest exemplar's up-rate crossed one half, after costs.
It counts winning trades of the exemplar calls and must be read beside the trade count, because a call that rarely flips makes few trades.
It tests the hard call from each exemplar's up-rate against the actual direction, and depends on the readout prior because most up-rates sit close to the training up share.
It shows whether the exemplar calls recover both up bars and down bars or simply call the side the training span favoured.
It condenses the four outcome cells of the exemplar calls into one number that stays at zero when every exemplar is called the same side.
It tests whether exemplars with a higher training up-rate are followed by more up bars, on a curve with one point per exemplar.
The readout is unweighted, so the gap between exemplar up-rates and realised up shares is a fair check, though the up-rates crowd into very few bins.
It shows how far the exemplar up-rates spread from the training up share; many small exemplar groups shrunk by the prior give almost no spread.
Each exemplar carries one up-rate, so the number of probability levels equals the number of exemplars visited and bounds what any ranking metric can show.
It shows whether the exemplar up-rates fall on both sides of one half or the model called one direction on nearly every bar.
The forecast is the shrunk mean scaled move of the training bars at the nearest exemplar, from a second fit of the same exemplars, tested against forecasting no move.
It is the size of the miss of the exemplar mean-move forecast in points, to be read beside the no-change forecast's error on the same bars.
It tests the sign of the exemplar mean move, but shrunk means often round to zero ticks, so the denominator shown with it can be small.

Both curves are the logarithmic loss of the exemplar up-rates, one on the training rows they were counted from and one on rows they never saw, so the difference is the readout's own overfit gap, which many small exemplar groups can widen.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The up-rate is a smoothed count and not a likelihood fit, and how far it can move from the training up share is set by the readout_prior_strength dial, so the number mostly grades that dial.
With long_only off and no stop or target the engine is never flat once in a trade, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not the exemplars.

caveats: The exemplars are fitted on at most maximum_fit_rows evenly spread training rows, so the states are those of a subsample of the training span.
When the messages do not settle the adapter retries with more damping and, if no exemplar emerges, falls back to one state at the training mean, which makes every probability the training up share.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so any interval needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the Micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its own close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

spectral_clustering_states.summary: Clusters of the nearest-neighbour graph of spread training bars, found in the eigenvectors of its Laplacian; new bars vote by their nearest fitted bars.
spectral_clustering_states.implementationNote: Bridge: spectral clustering (normalised Laplacian of the nearest-neighbour graph) on up to Maximum fit rows spread training rows; a new bar's cluster shares are a distance-weighted vote of its nearest fitted rows, and P(up) = those shares times each cluster's Beta-smoothed training up-rate. Differs from the spec: fitted on a subsample; new bars take their nearest clusters. Expect: probabilities near the base rate.

cluster_count.label: Clusters
cluster_count.description: How many clusters the spectral embedding is cut into.

affinity_neighbor_count.label: Graph neighbours
affinity_neighbor_count.description: Each fitted bar is linked to this many nearest bars in the affinity graph.

maximum_fit_rows.label: Maximum fit rows
maximum_fit_rows.description: At most this many training rows, spread evenly over the training span, enter spectral clustering (its cost grows with the square of the row count).

neighbor_count.label: Extension neighbours
neighbor_count.description: A new bar's cluster is a distance-weighted vote of this many nearest fitted bars.

readout_prior_strength.label: Readout prior strength
readout_prior_strength.description: How many pseudo-bars at the training base rate each state's up-rate (or mean move) is shrunk toward; a rarely visited state reads close to the base rate.

native.produces: A group label for every bar, obtained by linking each feature row to its most similar rows in a graph, placing the rows at coordinates given by the leading eigenvectors of that graph's normalised Laplacian, and cutting those coordinates into a chosen number of groups.
native.targetVariable: The feature row of a bar: which well connected region of the similarity graph of feature rows that bar belongs to, with no statement about the direction of the next move.
native.objectiveNote: Spectral clustering's version is the normalised cut of the similarity graph, relaxed so that the Laplacian's eigenvectors solve it, which lets groups be any shape as long as their members are chained together by near neighbours.

metrics.why: Measured in the eigenvector coordinates where the final cut is made, it tests whether the graph embedding really pulled the rows into tight, separate clumps; measured in raw feature space it would punish exactly the curved groups the graph was built to find.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the value for rows that sit as close to a neighbouring group as to their own in the embedding.

metrics.why: The neighbour graph changes when the neighbour count, the subsample of rows or the seed of the final cut changes, so two fits of the spectral clustering on shared bars must still place the same bars together for the groups to mean anything.
metrics.baseline: Zero, the value two unrelated groupings of the same bars reach by chance.

metrics.why: The graph is built from feature similarity alone, so the evidence that a connected region is a tradable condition is that bars inside it are followed by a different up share than the whole series.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series.

metrics.why: When the neighbour graph falls into disconnected pieces the eigenvectors isolate a few stray rows as their own groups and leave one giant group, and the share of bars per group makes that failure visible.

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: A unit-root test describes one input series before modelling and says nothing about how the similarity graph was cut.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: This belongs to fractional differencing of an input series; spectral clustering reads rows as points in a graph and keeps no memory.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: The Laplacian eigenvectors are chosen for graph connectivity and not for variance retained, so no variance share describes this embedding.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction Residual
notApplicable.why: Nothing in spectral clustering rebuilds a feature row, so a rebuild error was never a property of this model.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: Spectral clustering states no probability; a probability of up exists only after the Model Cycle attaches a training up-rate to each graph group.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: A cut of a similarity graph never takes a position, so it has no return stream of its own.

What trading the side of one half that the blended cluster up-rate fell on earned after costs under the engine's rule, read beside buy and hold on the same folds.
