self_organizing_map.summary: A Kohonen grid of prototypes trained by competitive learning on the training bars; a bar reads out its best-matching cell, smoothed over neighbouring cells.
self_organizing_map.implementationNote: Bridge: a MiniSom grid trained on the standardised training rows (Gaussian neighbourhood, decaying step, PCA start); a bar's state is its best-matching cell, whose training up-rate pools neighbouring cells with a Gaussian of Topology smoothing cells. Price: the pooled mean scaled move. Differs from the spec: the map's topology is used only for that pooling. Expect: near-base-rate probabilities.

grid_rows.label: Grid rows
grid_rows.description: Rows of the map's grid of cells.

grid_columns.label: Grid columns
grid_columns.description: Columns of the map's grid of cells.

neighborhood_width.label: Neighbourhood width
neighborhood_width.description: The initial width (in cells) of the Gaussian that drags a winner's neighbours along.

learning_rate.label: Learning rate
learning_rate.description: The initial step toward each training bar; it decays over training.

iteration_count.label: Training updates
iteration_count.description: How many single-bar updates train the map.

topology_smoothing.label: Topology smoothing
topology_smoothing.description: The readout pools each cell's evidence with its grid neighbours over this many cells (0: none).

readout_prior_strength.label: Readout prior strength
readout_prior_strength.description: How many pseudo-bars at the training base rate each state's up-rate (or mean move) is shrunk toward; a rarely visited state reads close to the base rate.

native.produces: A grid of prototype vectors laid out as a two-dimensional sheet, and for every bar the grid cell whose prototype is nearest to that bar's feature row, so that bars with similar features land in the same or neighbouring cells.
native.targetVariable: The position on the map grid of the best-matching cell for a bar's standardised feature row, a statement about which kind of market condition the bar resembles and never about where price goes next.
native.objectiveNote: The Kohonen update drags the winning cell and its grid neighbours toward each bar with a step and a neighbourhood width that both shrink, so the map minimises the distance from each bar to its nearest prototype only in the limit where the neighbourhood has shrunk to the winner alone, and before that it trades some of that distance for a smooth ordering of the sheet.

metrics.why: This is the map's quantisation error on bars it never trained on: each unseen bar is replaced by the prototype of its best-matching cell and the squared miss is taken as a share of the features' total spread, which shows whether the grid of prototypes still covers the market conditions of the next fold.
metrics.baseline: The same map with a single cell, whose prototype is the training mean of the features and whose error equals the whole feature variance.

metrics.why: The whole promise of a Kohonen grid over a plain set of centroids is that cells sitting next to each other hold similar bars, and this number counts the unseen bars whose nearest and second-nearest prototypes are not grid neighbours, which is where the sheet is folded or torn.

Read as a flattening of the feature space onto a sheet, the map is checked by asking whether bars that land in nearby cells were also close in the original features, so that a cluster seen on the grid picture is not a false neighbourhood created by the folding.

The reverse check of the sheet: bars that were close in the original features should still land in the same or adjoining cells, and a low share means the competitive updates split one market condition across distant corners of the grid.

The prototypes depend on the seeded random order in which training bars are shown and on the starting sheet, so two fits of the same grid on the same bars are compared after matching cells, and a low agreement means the cells are an accident of the draw order.
metrics.baseline: Agreement expected by chance between two unrelated assignments of the same bars to the same number of cells, which the index sets at zero.

metrics.why: The map never sees the outcome, so the test of whether its cells mean anything to a trader is whether the bars landing in a cell or a region of the grid are followed by an up share different from that of all scored bars of the same series.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series.

metrics.why: A grid has grid rows times grid columns cells and competitive learning can leave many of them without a single bar while a few winners take most of the tape, and the share of bars per cell shows how much of the sheet is actually used.
metrics.baseline: An even spread of the bars over every cell of the grid.

notApplicable.name: Wasserstein Distance
notApplicable.why: It never applied because the self-organising map produces prototypes and cell assignments and never generates a set of bars to compare with the real tape.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet Market Distance
notApplicable.why: It never applied because the self-organising map simulates no price trajectories and reads no order flow, so nothing exists to set beside the real paths.

notApplicable.name: Latent KL Divergence
notApplicable.why: It never applied because the map has no encoder distribution and no Gaussian prior; a bar's code is a single winning cell chosen by nearest distance.

notApplicable.name: Latent Uniformity
notApplicable.why: It never applied because the map's code is a cell on a flat grid and not a point on a hypersphere; the share of bars per cell is the map's own usage picture.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette coefficient
notApplicable.why: The map lays its cells out as one continuous sheet on purpose, so neighbouring cells hold nearly the same bars and a score that rewards groups for being far apart reads low for a well-ordered map; it applies only after the cells are merged into a few larger groups, which is a second clustering step and not the map.

notApplicable.name: Latent Kullback-Leibler divergence
notApplicable.why: A bar's code on the map is one hard cell index with no posterior distribution and no prior to be held close to, so there is no divergence term anywhere in the competitive update.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: Natively the map gives a cell and no probability of anything, so a score of stated odds has nothing to grade until a separate readout attaches an up share to each cell.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: The map groups bars and never takes a position, so a return per unit of risk describes whatever trading rule is bolted on afterwards and not the map.

asRun.standInNote: The map itself is the specified algorithm (a grid of prototypes trained by competitive learning with a Gaussian neighbourhood and a decaying step, started on the two leading principal components), but the specification stops at a cell per bar and gives no direction; the runnable adapter adds a readout that counts how often training bars in each cell were followed by an up move, pools that count over neighbouring cells and shrinks it toward the training up share, so every as-run number measures the map plus that counted readout and the map's topology is used only for the pooling.
asRun.probabilityNote: A bar is standardised with the training mean and deviation, sent to its best-matching cell, and given that cell's training up-rate, which is the up count pooled over grid neighbours with a Gaussian of topology smoothing cells and shrunk toward the fold's training up share by readout prior strength pseudo-bars; no validation curve is fitted and no class weighting is applied.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per scored bar, one value for the single fit

meaningful.why: The probability of up is a counted share per cell, so the bounded squared-miss score is the proper test of whether the up-rates the cells showed on training bars are repeated by the test bars that land in the same cells.

It is what the engine's rule earned after costs by going long whenever the bar's cell had a pooled training up-rate of at least one half and short otherwise, so it tests whether the side of one half a cell sits on carries over to unseen bars.

It asks whether cells with a higher training up-rate really collect more of the test bars that went up, using only the ordering of the cells; the curve has at most one point per occupied cell, so ties between bars in the same cell count half.

The readout is unweighted and has no validation curve, so the gap between a cell's stated up-rate and the up share of the test bars that land there is a direct check of whether the training frequencies were real or noise; it is read with the number of occupied bins, because the bin-weighted gap rests only on the bins that the cells' up-rates actually fill.

A slope below one says the cells' up-rates spread further from the training up share than the test bars justify, which is the signature of too little readout prior strength or too many cells for the bars available.

Neighbour pooling and the readout prior pull thinly visited cells toward the training up share, so the spread of the probability of up shows how far the populated cells actually commit away from that share, or whether the map quotes nearly the same number on every bar.

The model can state only one probability per occupied cell, at most grid rows times grid columns levels, and this count shows how many points the ranking and calibration curves really rest on in each fold.

With readout prior strength above zero no cell can read exactly zero or one, so a non-zero count means the prior was switched off and a thinly visited cell is quoting a certainty from a handful of training bars.

It summarises in one symmetric number the hard up or down vote each cell casts, and since the vote is cut at one half on an unweighted frequency it depends on which side of one half the fold's training up share happens to sit.

It is the share of scored bars whose cell voted the right way, to be read against the majority class accuracy and the predicted up share of the same fold, because a vote that simply follows the majority direction adds nothing over that reference.

This average of the up recall and the down recall shows whether the cells vote for both directions and are right when they do, and it is read beside the predicted up share and the majority class accuracy of the same fold.

It shows what share of bars fall in cells whose pooled up-rate is at least one half, and a value at zero or one means the map is trading a constant direction and every trading number is that direction's result.

It grades the steadiness of the per-bar result of trading the cells' votes under the engine's rule and costs, read beside the predicted up share and the trade count because a map that rarely changes its vote is close to holding one side.
It is the deepest fall of the equity from trading the cells' votes, and it shows what it cost when the market stayed in cells whose training up-rate pointed the wrong way.

It compares the money won with the money lost over trades that begin and end when a bar moves to a cell voting the other way, so it describes the map's switches between regions of the grid after costs.

A trade here lasts until the bar's cell flips its vote or a stop, target or fold end closes it, so the share of winning trades describes runs of same-vote cells and must be read with the average win and loss.
It counts how often consecutive bars moved between cells voting opposite ways, which tells whether the trading numbers rest on many switches or on a few long holds.
It sets the result of trading the cells' votes against simply holding the same instrument over the same folds, which is the reference a map that mostly votes up must beat.

The price forecast is a second fit of the same map-and-readout pipeline in which each cell reads its pooled and shrunk mean scaled move, so skill against the no-change forecast tests whether a cell's average training move says anything about the next move of bars landing there.

It is the size in points of the miss of the cell's mean move after it is multiplied back by the trailing move scale and rounded to the tick, to be read beside the no-change forecast error on the same bars.

It checks the sign of each cell's mean training move against the realised move, over the bars where the forecast is not rounded to zero ticks, and because the mean-move readout and the up-rate readout are separate fits their signs can disagree on the same bar.

The grid size, neighbourhood width, learning rate, topology smoothing and readout prior strength are picked inside each fold by this search score on training blocks and not by the map's quantisation error, so it is an optimistic selection score and never evidence of skill.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The probability is a counted share whose distance from zero and one is set by the readout prior strength dial and not by any likelihood the map was fitted to, so the logarithmic loss mostly reports that dial; the Brier score is the proper score for this readout.
With long only off and no stop or target the engine is always long or short once the first cell has voted, so the share of bars in the market describes the engine's rule and not the map.

Its reference is the up share of the scored test bars themselves, known only in hindsight, while the cells are shrunk toward the training up share, so a negative value can come from the base rate moving between training and test and not from the map.

caveats: The map's own native measures are not recorded as run: the quantisation error is computed on the training rows and written only into a log line, and the topographic error is not computed at all, so the as-run record cannot say how well the grid fits or how well it is ordered.

The fit is a single pass that reports one logarithmic loss of the smoothed readout on the training bars and one on the validation bars, both the same unweighted quantity; the training value is in-sample because the readout was counted on those same bars, nothing is selected on either number, and the validation bars are read only for that report.

The search inside each fold chooses the grid size and the other dials by the trading score of the readout on training blocks, so the kept grid is the one whose cells traded best there and not the one that maps the features best.
Consecutive scored bars share most of the bars inside their label horizon, so any interval around these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the Micro Nasdaq future the cost per side is that account's figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

Prototypes are compared with bars by straight-line distance over every standardised feature column at once, so the cells are dominated by whichever group of correlated features is largest and a bar's cell is a statement about that group.

isolation_forest_states.summary: How easily random trees isolate a bar, binned at training quantiles; each bin reads out what followed such bars in training.
isolation_forest_states.implementationNote: Bridge: isolation-forest path length (the anomaly score) binned at training quantiles, P(up) = the state's Beta-smoothed training up-rate. Differs from the spec: the score has no direction, so each bin is split by the side of the first principal axis (unsupervised, switchable off), which mostly sets up or down; the bin sets how strongly. Expect: near the base rate.

tree_count.label: Trees
tree_count.description: How many random isolation trees average the path length.

samples_per_tree.label: Samples per tree
samples_per_tree.description: Training bars drawn to grow each isolation tree.

bin_count.label: Score bins
bin_count.description: The anomaly score is cut into this many bins at the training rows' quantiles.

principal_axis_split.label: Split bins by the first principal axis
principal_axis_split.description: Split every score bin by the side of the training median along the training rows' first principal axis (an unsupervised half-space), so the readout can carry a direction.

readout_prior_strength.label: Readout prior strength
readout_prior_strength.description: How many pseudo-bars at the training base rate each state's up-rate (or mean move) is shrunk toward; a rarely visited state reads close to the base rate.

native.produces: One unsigned anomaly score per bar, computed from the average number of random splits the isolation trees need before the bar sits alone in a leaf, where a short path means the bar is unusual.
native.targetVariable: How unlike the training bars this bar's feature row is, measured by how quickly random feature cuts isolate it, with no statement about whether price goes up or down afterwards
native.objectiveNote: Nothing is minimised here: every tree picks a random feature and a random cut value, and the score is simply the averaged path length rescaled by the expected path length of a random search tree of the same sample size.

metrics.why: With no labelled anomalies on a futures tape, the only honest test of a short isolation path is whether the bars the trees isolate quickly are followed by a larger absolute move over the label horizon than the bars that take many cuts to isolate.
metrics.baseline: The mean absolute forward move of all scored bars of the same series

metrics.why: The trees are grown from random features, random cut values and a random subsample, so the same bars should stay at the short-path end of the ranking when the forest is regrown with another seed or on the next fold's training span.
metrics.baseline: The same forest regrown with a different seed on the same training bars

metrics.why: The path-length cut is placed so that the configured contamination share of training bars falls beyond it, so a very different share of test bars beyond the same cut shows the test features have drifted away from the bars the trees were grown on.
metrics.baseline: The contamination share configured for the forest

notApplicable.name: Stationarity ADF p-Value
notApplicable.why: A unit-root test describes a time series, while the isolation trees score each feature row on its own and produce no series whose stationarity is a property of the model.

notApplicable.name: Memory Retention Ratio
notApplicable.why: It belongs to fractional differencing of a price series; random feature cuts keep or discard no memory, so the ratio never described this model.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette Score
notApplicable.why: The forest gives a ranking of how easily each bar is isolated and forms no clusters, so there are no groups whose tightness could be measured.

notApplicable.name: Explained Variance Ratio
notApplicable.why: No projection or regression is fitted, so there is no variance that the isolation trees could be said to explain.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction Residual
notApplicable.why: The trees never rebuild the feature row from a compressed code, so there is no rebuilt input to subtract from the real one.

notApplicable.name: Accuracy of the direction call
notApplicable.why: A path length through random trees says how strange a bar is and carries no sign, so natively there is no up or down call to count as right or wrong.

notApplicable.name: Precision, recall and F-one score against labelled anomalies
notApplicable.why: The specification proposes them only if ground-truth anomaly labels exist, and no such labels exist for market bars, so there is nothing to count the flagged bars against.

notApplicable.name: Assignment stability
notApplicable.why: It compares two partitions and throws away the ordering of the path lengths, which is the whole output of the forest; the rank stability of the score is the right check.

asRun.standInNote: The isolation forest itself is fitted as the specification describes, on the fold's standardised training rows without labels, but its path-length score has no direction, so the runnable adapter cuts the score into bin_count bins at the training quantiles, splits every bin by the side of the training median along the first principal axis of the training rows, and quotes each resulting state's Beta-smoothed training up-rate; every as-run number therefore measures the forest plus that readout, and the up or down side comes mostly from the principal-axis half while the path length only sets how strongly.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the up share of the training bars that fell in the same state, where a state is one training-quantile bin of the isolation-forest path-length score crossed with one side of the first principal axis, and the share is pulled toward the fold's training up-rate by a Beta prior whose weight is readout_prior_strength, with no class weighting and no validation curve.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per labelled bar, one value for the single fit; the training value is in-sample because the state up-rates were counted from those same training bars, the logged step minimises nothing, and the fit of the price readout logs the mean absolute error in volatility-scaled move units instead

meaningful.why: It grades the handful of smoothed up-rates the path-length states quote, on a bounded scale that suits a counted share, and shows whether knowing a bar's isolation bin and principal-axis side beat quoting the fold's training up share on every bar.

It is the closest engine number to the native question, because it measures whether bars in different path-length states really went up at different rates on the test span or whether every state landed on the same up share.

The readout is an unweighted training frequency, so it is a real claim against the base rate, and the binned gap shows whether the up-rate each isolation state had in training was repeated on the test bars; it is read with the occupied-bin count because the states quote only a few levels near one half.

It shows how far the state up-rates move from their average, which the Beta prior and the weak link between isolation depth and direction keep small, so a value near zero means the model is quoting the base rate.

It tests whether states with a higher training up-rate went up more often on the test span, but the forest's readout takes at most twice bin_count distinct values, so the curve has only a few points and the level count may be small.

It counts how many different up-rates the path-length states actually quoted in a fold, which is capped at twice bin_count and tells the reader how coarse every ranking and calibration number for this model is.

It is the share of scored bars where the state's training majority direction matched the actual move, and because the side of the first principal axis decides most calls it largely tests whether that unsupervised half-space kept its training lean.
It shows whether calling the majority direction of each isolation state beat calling the fold's training majority direction on every bar, which is the bar this readout is expected to sit close to.
It averages how often the state call caught the up bars and the down bars, so a readout in which every path-length state leans the same way as the training span earns no credit.
It puts the four cells of the state call into one symmetric number, and since the fit is unweighted the cut at one half carries the training up share of each isolation state and no fitted prior.

It is what trading the majority direction of the current isolation state earned after costs under the engine's rule of following the latest call and filling at the next bar's open, read beside buy and hold on the same folds.

It is the per-bar reward for risk of trading the state call, and it depends only on which side of one half each state's up-rate fell, so it tests the principal-axis side far more than the depth at which the trees isolated the bar.
It is the deepest fall of the equity from trading the state call, and it shows the cost of a stretch in which the up-lean each isolation state had in training reversed on the test bars.
It compares dollars won with dollars lost over the trades that close when a bar moves into a state with the opposite lean, after costs, as a description of the engine's rule applied to this readout.
It is the share of closed trades that ended positive, where a trade ends when the isolation state's call changes side, a stop or target is hit or the fold ends, so it is read with the trade count.

It grades a second fit of the same forest whose states read out the shrunk mean scaled move that followed them in training, against forecasting no move on the same resolved bars, and so tests whether isolation states carry any expected move at all.

It is the typical miss in points of the state mean-move readout after tick rounding, which sits close to the no-change forecast's error because the shrunk state means are small beside a typical horizon move.

It is how often the sign of the state's mean training move matched the actual move, counted only where both are non-zero after tick rounding, and small state means round to zero on many bars so the denominator must be read with it.

It is the selection score that chose tree_count, samples_per_tree, bin_count and readout_prior_strength inside each fold's training span, optimistic by construction and not a property of the isolation trees.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The readout is a counted share whose distance from zero and one is set by the readout_prior_strength dial and not by the isolation trees, so the size of this loss reflects the prior more than the model and the Brier score is the proper score read for it.
With long_only off and no stop or target the engine is always in a position once the first state call is made, so the share describes the engine's rule and not the forest.

caveats: The up or down side of the call comes mostly from the first-principal-axis half each score bin is split by, an unsupervised direction that is switchable off, so good or bad results are not evidence about isolation depth alone.
The path-length cut for the contamination share named in the specification is never applied as run, because the adapter bins the whole score at training quantiles and flags no bars.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so any interval on these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the Micro Nasdaq future the cost per side is the Micro Nasdaq account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

local_outlier_factor_states.summary: A bar's local density against its nearest training bars (novelty mode), binned at training quantiles; each bin reads out what followed such bars.
local_outlier_factor_states.implementationNote: Bridge: the local outlier factor of a bar against its nearest fitted training rows (novelty mode, never test rows) binned at training quantiles, P(up) = the state's Beta-smoothed training up-rate. Differs from the spec: the score has no direction, so each bin is split by the side of the first principal axis (unsupervised, switchable off), which mostly sets up or down; the bin sets how strongly. Expect: near the base rate.

neighbor_count.label: Neighbours
neighbor_count.description: The local density is measured over this many nearest training bars.

maximum_fit_rows.label: Maximum fit rows
maximum_fit_rows.description: At most this many training rows, spread evenly over the training span, enter the neighbour set (its cost grows with the square of the row count).

bin_count.label: Score bins
bin_count.description: The anomaly score is cut into this many bins at the training rows' quantiles.

principal_axis_split.label: Split bins by the first principal axis
principal_axis_split.description: Split every score bin by the side of the training median along the training rows' first principal axis (an unsupervised half-space), so the readout can carry a direction.

readout_prior_strength.label: Readout prior strength
readout_prior_strength.description: How many pseudo-bars at the training base rate each state's up-rate (or mean move) is shrunk toward; a rarely visited state reads close to the base rate.

native.produces: One unsigned outlier factor per bar, the average local reachability density of the bar's nearest neighbours divided by the bar's own, where a value well above one means the bar sits in a much emptier region than its neighbours do.
native.targetVariable: How sparse the neighbourhood of this bar's feature row is compared with the neighbourhoods of its nearest rows, with no statement about the direction of the next move
native.objectiveNote: Nothing is trained or minimised: the factor is computed directly from distances to the nearest rows, and the only choices are the neighbour count and the distance measure.

metrics.why: A futures tape has no labelled outliers, so the test of a high density ratio is whether bars sitting in emptier neighbourhoods than their nearest rows are followed by a larger absolute move over the label horizon than bars in crowded neighbourhoods.
metrics.baseline: The mean absolute forward move of all scored bars of the same series

metrics.why: The density ratio of a bar depends on which rows happen to be its nearest neighbours, so the ranking should survive a change of the reference rows from one fold's training span to the next and a modest change of the neighbour count.
metrics.baseline: The same factor computed against the adjacent fold's training rows on the shared bars

metrics.why: The cut on the outlier factor is placed so the configured contamination share of fitted rows lies above it, so a much larger share of unseen bars above that cut means the new bars fall in regions the stored neighbours never covered.
metrics.baseline: The contamination share configured for the detector

notApplicable.name: Realized Sharpe Ratio
notApplicable.why: A density ratio against nearest rows never takes a position, so natively there is no stream of returns to divide by its spread.

notApplicable.name: Sortino Ratio
notApplicable.why: With no position there are no losing bars whose size could form the downside risk in the denominator.

notApplicable.name: Maximum Drawdown
notApplicable.why: The outlier factor produces no equity curve, so there is no peak to fall from until the engine trades a readout of it.

notApplicable.name: Profit Factor
notApplicable.why: The detector opens and closes no trades, so there are no winning and losing dollars to compare.

notApplicable.name: Half-Kelly Sizing
notApplicable.why: Position sizing needs an edge and odds, and a measure of how sparse a bar's neighbourhood is supplies neither.

notApplicable.name: Policy Entropy
notApplicable.why: The row belongs to a reinforcement-learning table; this method has no policy and chooses no action.

notApplicable.name: Accuracy of the direction call
notApplicable.why: A ratio of neighbourhood densities says how isolated a bar is and has no sign, so natively there is no up or down call to grade.

notApplicable.name: Precision, recall and F-one score against labelled anomalies
notApplicable.why: The specification offers them only when ground-truth anomaly labels are available, and market bars carry no such labels.

mixture_model_regimes.summary: Class-conditional Gaussian mixtures of up and down training bars joined by Bayes' rule, or one mixture of regimes read out by their up-rates.
mixture_model_regimes.implementationNote: Bridge: class-conditional mode fits a Gaussian mixture to up and one to down training rows (standardised features or their principal components); P(up|x) = pi_up f_up / (pi_up f_up + pi_down f_down), then a logistic curve on validation. Regime mode reads one mixture out by up-rates. Differs from the spec: the DPM prior is the Dirichlet process key. Expect: over-confident densities tamed by the curve.

mixture_mode.label: Mode
mixture_mode.description: class_conditional: one mixture per outcome and Bayes' rule; regime_posterior: one mixture of regimes read out by their up-rates.

component_count.label: Components
component_count.description: Gaussian components per mixture (per class in class-conditional mode).

covariance_structure.label: Covariance structure
covariance_structure.description: Each component's covariance: full (any ellipsoid) or diagonal (axis-aligned).

covariance_regularization.label: Covariance regularization
covariance_regularization.description: Added to every covariance diagonal so a component never collapses onto a few bars.

principal_component_count.label: Principal components
principal_component_count.description: The mixture runs on this many leading principal components of the standardised training rows (whitened); 0 uses every standardised feature.

readout_prior_strength.label: Readout prior strength
readout_prior_strength.description: How many pseudo-bars at the training base rate each state's up-rate (or mean move) is shrunk toward; a rarely visited state reads close to the base rate.

native.produces: A probability density over feature rows built as a weighted sum of Gaussian components, and for every bar the posterior share of responsibility each component takes for it.
native.targetVariable: How likely a feature row is under the fitted mixture and which component most plausibly generated it; the output says nothing about the direction of the coming price move.
native.objectiveNote: The mixture's likelihood is climbed by expectation-maximisation, which alternates between sharing each bar among the components and refitting each component's weight, mean and covariance in closed form, and it stops at a local peak that depends on the starting point.

metrics.why: Expectation-maximisation only ever raises the likelihood of the training bars, so the honest test is the mean log density the fitted components give to bars outside the trailing window they were fitted on.
metrics.baseline: The same mixture reduced to a single Gaussian component fitted on the same training bars.

metrics.why: A component that collapses onto a handful of bars drives the training likelihood upward without limit, and a held-out log density far below the training one is how that collapse shows up.

The components are identified only up to a reshuffle of their labels and each restart can end on a different local peak, so the component a bar mostly belongs to must agree across restarts and adjacent windows.
metrics.baseline: Chance agreement between two labelings, which the adjusted Rand index scores as zero.

metrics.why: A component matters to a trader only if the bars it takes most responsibility for are followed by an up share different from the series as a whole.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series.

metrics.why: The mixing weights show whether the component count chosen by the information criterion is really used or whether one bell holds nearly every bar while the others sit on slivers.
The mixture treats bars as independent draws, so the run length of the leading component checks whether its components happen to be lasting market conditions or flicker from bar to bar.

notApplicable.name: fANOVA Variance Explained
notApplicable.why: It describes how much each hyperparameter moved a tuning score, which is a property of a search and not of the fitted density.

notApplicable.name: SHAP Stability Score
notApplicable.why: The mixture maps a row to a density and to responsibilities, not to a prediction with per-feature attributions, so there is nothing to attribute.

notApplicable.name: Expected Calibration Error
notApplicable.why: Natively no probability of an up move is stated, so there are no stated odds to hold against observed up shares.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette coefficient
notApplicable.why: The components are stretched ellipses that overlap and share bars by responsibility, and the silhouette assumes round groups with one owner per bar.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: Natively the mixture is a density of feature rows fitted without labels, so it states no probability of an up move to score.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio

asRun.standInNote: The specification describes one unsupervised mixture of all bars, while the runnable adapter in its default mixture_mode fits one Gaussian mixture to the up-labelled training rows and another to the down-labelled rows, joins them by Bayes' rule with the training class shares and reshapes the result with a logistic curve fitted on validation rows; the as-run numbers therefore measure a generative classifier built from two mixtures, and only the alternative regime mode fits the single label-free mixture and reads it out by up-rates.
asRun.probabilityNote: The raw probability of up is the summed posterior responsibility of the components fitted on up rows, which is Bayes' rule over the two class densities with the training class shares as priors, and the reported probability is a logistic curve of the log-odds of that value whose slope and intercept are fitted on the fold's validation rows.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per bar, one value for the single fit: the logarithmic loss of the raw Bayes posterior of the two class mixtures (or of the regime readout in regime mode) on the training rows, then the logarithmic loss of the validation-curve-reshaped probability on the validation rows

meaningful.why: It scores the Bayes posterior of the two class mixtures after the validation-fitted curve has tamed their overconfident density ratio, on test bars that neither the mixtures nor the curve saw.

The ranking of bars comes from the ratio of the up-row mixture's density to the down-row mixture's density and is untouched by the curve unless its slope turns negative, so this tests the two densities themselves.
A bounded score of the curve-reshaped posterior, useful because raw Gaussian density ratios in many dimensions run to near certainty and the curve may not pull every bar back.

The class priors are the training shares and the curve is fitted without weights, so comparing the reshaped posterior with observed up shares is a fair check of the curve fitted on the validation rows.
It measures on test bars whether the slope the curve learned on the validation rows still shrinks the two mixtures' log-odds by the right amount.
It shows how much spread the curve left in the posterior; a curve slope near zero flattens the two mixtures into a constant and makes every other probability number trivial.
It is what trading long whenever the curve-reshaped posterior of the two class mixtures reached one half, and short otherwise, earned after costs under the engine's rule.
It relates the per-bar profit of the calls from the two class mixtures to its variability; zero is an arithmetic marker and not a no-skill reference, because a random caller pays costs.
It shows the deepest loss run while the position followed whichever class mixture claimed the bar after the curve was applied.
It compares winning and losing dollars of the trades opened each time the reshaped posterior crossed one half, after costs.
It counts winning trades among the stretches between flips of the two-mixture call and is read beside the trade count, since each flip pays a round trip.
It tests the hard call at one half of the reshaped posterior, a cut whose position is set by the curve's intercept fitted on validation rows and not by the mixtures alone.
It shows whether the two class mixtures recover up bars and down bars alike or whether the curve's intercept pushed nearly every call to one side.
It condenses the four outcome cells of the two-mixture call into one symmetric number that stays at zero when the curve leaves every bar on the same side of one half.
It shows how the curve's intercept split the calls between long and short and is read beside every trading number of this model.

The forecast comes from a second fit in which one mixture is fitted to rows whose scaled move was positive and one to the rest, each component reading out its shrunk mean move, tested against forecasting no move; no curve is applied to it.
It is the typical miss in points of that responsibility-weighted blend of component mean moves, to be read beside the no-change forecast's error on the same bars.
It tests the sign of the blended component mean move from the second fit, which is not the call that is traded and often rounds to zero ticks, so its denominator can be small.

The search picks the mixture_mode itself on each fold's training span together with the component count and covariance dials, so this selection score also tells which of the two mechanisms a fold ended up running.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The training figure is the logarithmic loss of the raw Bayes posterior on the rows the two mixtures were fitted on, and the validation figure is taken after a curve fitted on those same validation rows, so the difference compares two different quantities.
With long_only off and no stop or target the engine is never flat once in a trade, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not the mixtures.

caveats: The mixture_mode dial is searched, so one fold can run the two class mixtures with Bayes' rule and the next a single label-free mixture read out by Beta-smoothed up-rates, and a run's numbers can mix the two mechanisms.
The curve's slope and intercept are fitted on the fold's validation rows, so the validation loss shown for the fit is partly in sample and only the test walk is out of sample.
A fitted curve with a negative slope inverts the call of the two mixtures, and the fitted slope is written to the run log only.
The label-free likelihood the specification scores is not recorded in either mode.
Expectation-maximisation is started once per mixture and may stop at its iteration limit, so the components are one local solution.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so any interval needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the Micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its own close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

dirichlet_process_regimes.summary: A truncated stick-breaking Dirichlet-process mixture of the training bars that decides how many regimes it needs; each regime reads out its up-rate.
dirichlet_process_regimes.implementationNote: Bridge: a Dirichlet-process Gaussian mixture (stick-breaking, truncated variational inference) on standardised training rows infers how many regimes carry weight; P(up) = sum over regimes of the bar's responsibility times the regime's Beta-smoothed training up-rate. Price: the same sum over mean scaled moves. Differs from the spec: variational, not Gibbs, and truncated at Truncation level. Expect: a few regimes; probabilities near the base rate.

truncation_level.label: Truncation level
truncation_level.description: The most components the stick-breaking prior may use; unused ones keep near-zero weight.

concentration.label: Concentration
concentration.description: The Dirichlet process's alpha: larger opens new regimes more readily.

covariance_structure.label: Covariance structure
covariance_structure.description: Each component's covariance: full (any ellipsoid) or diagonal (axis-aligned).

covariance_regularization.label: Covariance regularization
covariance_regularization.description: Added to every covariance diagonal so a component never collapses onto a few bars.

readout_prior_strength.label: Readout prior strength
readout_prior_strength.description: How many pseudo-bars at the training base rate each state's up-rate (or mean move) is shrunk toward; a rarely visited state reads close to the base rate.

native.produces: A posterior over how the bars split into regimes: stick-breaking weights for an open-ended list of Gaussian components, each bar's share of responsibility per component, and the number of components that end up carrying weight.
native.targetVariable: Which regime generated each feature row, how many regimes the data support and how likely a row is under the resulting mixture density; nothing in the output states the direction of the coming price move.
native.objectiveNote: The Dirichlet process adds a prior over the number of components itself, so the fit weighs partitions with few and with many regimes by how well each explains the bars, using collapsed Gibbs sampling over the Chinese restaurant process or a truncated stick-breaking variational approximation.

metrics.why: The stick-breaking mixture is a density, so the honest test of the regimes it opened is the mean log density it gives to bars that arrived after the window it was inferred on.
metrics.baseline: The same model restricted to a single Gaussian component fitted on the same training bars, which is the no-clustering reference the specification names.

metrics.why: The whole promise of the stick-breaking prior is that the data decide how many sticks hold weight, and the share of bars per regime shows that count and exposes singleton regimes opened on a few heavy-tailed noise bars.

The sampler relabels regimes freely from one sweep or seed to the next, so the partition has to be compared after matching components by their means, and a partition that changes between seeds is not a regime map.
metrics.baseline: Chance agreement between two labelings, which the adjusted Rand index scores as zero.

metrics.why: A regime the concentration parameter allowed to open earns its place for a trader only if the bars assigned to it are followed by an up share different from the series as a whole.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series.

metrics.why: The process treats bars as exchangeable and ignores their order, so the run length of the leading regime checks whether its clusters are lasting market conditions or labels that flicker from bar to bar.

The specification asks for several Gibbs chains from different seeds, and the count of active regimes should be reported only when those chains agree on it, because the sampler mixes slowly when regimes sit close together.

notApplicable.name: fANOVA Variance Explained
notApplicable.why: It apportions a tuning score among hyperparameters of a search, which describes the search and not the posterior over partitions.

notApplicable.name: SHAP Stability Score
notApplicable.why: The process predicts no outcome from features, so there are no feature attributions whose stability could be measured.

notApplicable.name: Expected Calibration Error
notApplicable.why: Natively the model states no probability of an up move, so there are no stated odds to compare with observed up shares.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette coefficient
notApplicable.why: The regimes are overlapping Gaussian components that share bars by responsibility, and the silhouette assumes compact groups with one owner per bar.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: Natively the process is inferred without labels and states no probability of an up move, so there is nothing for a direction score to grade.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: A regime label is not a position; a trading result exists only after the Model Cycle attaches an up-rate to each regime.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter infers a truncated stick-breaking Gaussian mixture on standardised training rows by variational inference, not by the Gibbs sampler the specification leads with, and without labels; the up or down call is added by a readout that gives every regime a Beta-smoothed training up-rate, so each as-run number measures the mixture plus that readout and the mixture's own log-likelihood is not recorded.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the sum over stick-breaking components of the bar's posterior responsibility times that component's responsibility-weighted training up-rate, each up-rate pulled toward the fold's training up share by the readout_prior_strength dial.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per bar, one value for the single fit: the logarithmic loss of the Beta-smoothed regime readout on the training rows, then the logarithmic loss of the same uncalibrated readout on the validation rows

meaningful.why: The probability of up blends smoothed regime up-rates by responsibility, and the bounded squared-error score tests whether the up-rates learned on training bars still hold on bars the mixture never saw.
Soft responsibilities make the blended probability continuous, so this tests whether bars leaning toward regimes with a high training up-rate really go up more often.
It is what trading long whenever the responsibility-weighted blend of regime up-rates reached one half, and short otherwise, earned after costs under the engine's rule.
It relates the per-bar profit of the blended regime calls to its variability; zero is an arithmetic marker and not a no-skill reference, because a random caller pays costs.
It shows the deepest loss run while the position followed whichever side the blend of regime up-rates favoured, including stretches spent in a regime whose training up-rate no longer held.
It compares winning and losing dollars of the trades opened each time the blended regime up-rate crossed one half, after costs.
It counts winning trades of the blended calls and must be read beside the trade count, because a blend that hovers near one half flips often and pays costs on every flip.
It tests the hard call from the blended regime up-rate against the actual direction, a call that turns on small departures from the training up share.
It shows whether the blended calls recover up bars and down bars alike or simply take the side that every weighty regime favours.
It condenses the four outcome cells of the blended calls into one number that stays at zero when the blend never crosses one half.
The readout is unweighted, so the gap between blended up-rates and realised up shares is a fair check, though the blend stays close to the training up share and fills few bins.
It checks without bins whether the small departures of the blended up-rate from the training up share are the right size on unseen bars, which is what the readout_prior_strength shrinkage decides.

The single fit reports the logarithmic loss of the same unweighted regime readout on the training rows and on the validation rows, so their difference shows whether the smoothed regime up-rates learned on training bars held up on the bars that followed.
Averaging regime up-rates by responsibility and shrinking each toward the base rate pulls every bar toward the middle, and this shows how much spread survives.
It shows whether the blended up-rate fell on both sides of one half or the regimes that carry weight all lean the same way, which makes every call the same.
The forecast is the responsibility-weighted sum of each regime's shrunk mean scaled move, from a second fit of the same mixture, tested against forecasting no move.
It is the size of the miss of the blended regime mean-move forecast in points, to be read beside the no-change forecast's error on the same bars.
It tests the sign of the blended regime mean move, but that blend is small and often rounds to zero ticks, so the denominator shown with it can be small.

It is the search score under which the concentration, the covariance dials and the readout shrinkage were picked on each fold's training span; it is a selection score, optimistic by construction, and not a result.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The blended up-rate comes from smoothed counts and not from a likelihood fit to the labels, and its distance from the training up share is set by the readout_prior_strength dial, so the number mostly grades that dial.
With long_only off and no stop or target the engine is never flat once in a trade, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not the mixture.

caveats: The mixture's own held-out log-likelihood is not computed, and the count of regimes that carry weight is written to the run log only, so the native result cannot be read from the scoreboard.
The truncation_level and iteration_count dials are not searched, and variational inference may stop at its iteration limit, which the run log states, so the regimes are one approximate solution.
A stick-breaking component that no training bar visits keeps a near-zero weight and reads the training up share, so unused components add nothing but also cost nothing.
The price forecast comes from a second fit of the same mixture, so forecast numbers and direction numbers describe two separately fitted sets of regimes.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so any interval needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the Micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its own close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

hidden_markov_regimes.summary: A Gaussian hidden Markov model of the training span's bars; each bar's forward-filtered state weights the states' training up-rates.
hidden_markov_regimes.implementationNote: Bridge: a diagonal Gaussian HMM fitted by Baum-Welch on the training span (leading principal components); P(up) = sum over states of the forward-filtered probability at the bar times the state's training up-rate weighted by filtered probabilities. Differs from the spec: forward filter only, never the smoother. Expect: regime persistence is the whole edge.

state_count.label: Hidden states
state_count.description: How many hidden market states the chain moves between.

iteration_count.label: Baum-Welch iterations
iteration_count.description: EM passes over the training span.

principal_component_count.label: Principal components
principal_component_count.description: The emission model runs on this many leading principal components of the standardised training rows (whitened); 0 uses every standardised feature.

readout_prior_strength.label: Readout prior strength
readout_prior_strength.description: How many pseudo-bars at the training base rate each state's up-rate (or mean move) is shrunk toward; a rarely visited state reads close to the base rate.

native.produces: For every bar a probability over a small set of hidden regimes (the causal filtered posterior, or the most likely regime path for offline labelling), together with a Gaussian emission density per regime and a transition matrix.
native.targetVariable: the unobserved market regime behind each bar's feature row, and the probability of the next bar's regime given the current one
native.objectiveNote: The likelihood is of the whole feature sequence, maximised by the Baum-Welch expectation-maximisation loop, so the transition matrix is fitted jointly with the emission densities and persistence is part of the objective.

metrics.why: Baum-Welch climbs the log-likelihood of the training sequence, and the forward filter's one-step-ahead log density on unseen bars tells whether the fitted regimes and their transition matrix describe new bars or only the window they were carved from.
metrics.baseline: The same model with a single state, which is one Gaussian over the feature rows

metrics.why: Expectation-maximisation stops at a local optimum that depends on the starting transition matrix and means, so regime labels from two restarts or two adjacent folds must agree on shared bars before a regime can be named.
The regimes are fitted to feature rows with no view of what price did next, so the up share and the size of the following move inside each filtered regime show whether the regimes matter for trading.
metrics.baseline: The up share of all scored bars of the same series

metrics.why: The diagonal of the transition matrix implies how many bars a regime lasts, and a fitted regime that hands over every bar or two has carved noise rather than a market condition.
Too many states let the fit park a handful of bars in a near-singular regime, and the share of bars each regime holds exposes that before its emission covariance is trusted.
The per-bar log-likelihood is the same quantity on the training window and on later bars, so the drop between them measures how much of the regime structure was fitted to one window.

notApplicable.name: fANOVA Variance Explained
notApplicable.why: This decomposes a hyperparameter search surface and says nothing about the regimes, the emission densities or the transition matrix the model fits.

notApplicable.name: SHAP Stability Score
notApplicable.why: The model explains bars through a regime label and that regime's emission mean, not through per-feature attributions, so there is no attribution to stabilise.

notApplicable.name: Expected Calibration Error
notApplicable.why: Natively the model states a probability over hidden regimes that are never observed, so no outcome exists to compare a stated probability against.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette coefficient
notApplicable.why: A regime is defined by which regime came before it as much as by where its feature rows sit, so a distance-only tightness score misjudges states that overlap in feature space.

notApplicable.name: Accuracy
notApplicable.why: The hidden regimes carry no up or down meaning and the true regime is never observed, so there is no label a hit rate could be counted against.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: A regime posterior takes no position; a return per unit of risk describes whatever trading rule is later attached to the regimes.

asRun.standInNote: The hidden Markov model itself is the specification's: diagonal Gaussian emissions fitted by Baum-Welch on the training span and read through the forward filter only. The up or down call is an added readout, each regime's smoothed training up share weighted by the filtered regime probabilities, so every as-run number measures the regimes plus that readout and none of them is the model's own objective.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the sum over regimes of the forward-filtered probability of the regime at the bar times that regime's training up share, shrunk toward the training base rate by readout_prior_strength pseudo-bars; no curve is fitted on validation rows.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per bar, one value for the single fit, the unweighted logarithmic loss of the readout probability of up on the training rows and on the validation rows

meaningful.why: The stated number is a blend of a few per-regime training up shares, a frequency estimate that was never validated, and this bounded proper score grades how well that blend matched what followed.
The call flips only when the forward filter moves its weight to a regime whose training up share lies on the other side of one half, so this is what trading regime switches earned after costs.
Return per unit of bar-to-bar variation from holding the side that the currently filtered regime favoured in training, under the engine's rule with costs.
Persistent regimes mean long holds, and the deepest equity fall shows the price of a regime whose training lean did not repeat on the test bars.
Winning against losing trade totals for trades that open and close on filtered regime switches, each trade spanning one stay in a regime group.
The share of regime-switch trades that closed with a gain, read with the trade count because sticky regimes close only a few trades per fold.
Counts how often the filtered regime weight crossed between an up-leaning and a down-leaning regime, the only event that makes this model trade.
The hit rate of calling up whenever the filtered blend of regime up shares is at or above one half, which tests whether a regime's training lean holds on unseen bars.
When every regime's training up share sits on the same side of one half the model makes one call throughout, and averaging the hit rate over up bars and down bars exposes that.
One number for whether the regime-driven call moves with the realised direction, which is zero when the regimes never disagree about the side.
The filtered probabilities blend the per-regime up shares continuously, so ranking bars by the blend tests whether bars the filter places more firmly in an up-leaning regime go up more often.

The readout is unweighted and shrunk toward the training base rate, so the gap between the blended up share and the observed up share shows whether training regime frequencies carried over; few bins are occupied.
A slope away from one shows whether the spread between the regimes' training up shares was too wide or too narrow for the test bars, without relying on bins.
Per-regime up shares shrunk toward the base rate differ little, and the spread of the stated probability shows whether the regimes say anything different from each other about direction.
Shows the share of bars the filter spent in up-leaning regimes, which is the whole of the model's positioning.
The forecast is each regime's shrunk mean training move weighted by the filtered regime probabilities, so this tests whether the regimes' average moves beat assuming no move.
The typical miss in price points of the filtered blend of per-regime mean moves, which is small in size and therefore close to the no-change miss.
The hit rate of the sign of the blended regime mean move on bars where the tick-rounded forecast is not zero, a denominator that can be small because the blend is often under one tick.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The stated number is a smoothed count from the training span rather than a fitted likelihood, so the proper score for it is the Brier score and this one grades a quantity the readout never optimised.
With the default dials the engine is always long or short once the first call is made, so the share of bars in a position describes the engine's rule and not the regimes.

The logged training and validation losses are the same quantity, the logarithmic loss of the readout probability of up, so their difference is a readout overfit gap that shows how far the regimes' training up shares fail to carry over; it is not the gap in the regime model's own objective, the likelihood of the feature sequence.

caveats: The emission model runs on the leading principal components of the standardised training rows, so regimes are defined in that reduced space and not on the full feature row.
The regime model never sees a label; direction enters only through the per-regime training up share, so a fold in which no regime leans away from the base rate produces one constant call.
Prediction uses the forward filter only, so a bar's regime probability reads rows up to that bar and never the smoothed posterior.
The logged training loss is in-sample for the readout, because each regime's up share was counted on the same training rows that the loss is then computed on.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label looks several bars ahead, so intervals around any of these numbers need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance.
For roots other than the Micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its own close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

scenario_analysis.summary: Historical scenarios found in the training bars, each with a driver table and an outcome table; today's bar is weighted across scenarios by how much it resembles each.
scenario_analysis.implementationNote: Bridge: scenarios are Gaussian-mixture components on the training rows' leading principal components, their count chosen by BIC; each keeps a driver table and an outcome table (up-rate, scaled-move quantiles); P(up) = sum of scenario weights times up-rates, then a logistic curve on validation. Differs from the spec: scenarios are historical, not hand-written. Expect: near the base rate.

scenario_count.label: Most scenarios
scenario_count.description: BIC picks the scenario count between 2 and this.

covariance_structure.label: Covariance structure
covariance_structure.description: Each component's covariance: full (any ellipsoid) or diagonal (axis-aligned).

covariance_regularization.label: Covariance regularization
covariance_regularization.description: Added to every covariance diagonal so a component never collapses onto a few bars.

principal_component_count.label: Principal components
principal_component_count.description: The scenario mixture runs on this many leading principal components of the standardised training rows (whitened); 0 uses every standardised feature.

readout_prior_strength.label: Readout prior strength
readout_prior_strength.description: How many pseudo-bars at the training base rate each state's up-rate (or mean move) is shrunk toward; a rarely visited state reads close to the base rate.

native.produces: A side-by-side table giving, for each of a handful of named and internally consistent scenarios, the profit and loss and risk impact the current book would suffer if that scenario's stated driver shocks occurred.
native.targetVariable: The conditional revaluation of the current positions under each authored set of driver shocks, with no statement about which scenario will happen
native.objectiveNote: The scenarios and their shock sizes are written by a person; the only estimated part is the sensitivity mapping from driver moves to instrument moves, which the specification fits by ordinary least-squares regression on a rolling window.

metrics.why: The sensitivity mapping from driver moves to instrument moves is the only estimated part of scenario analysis, and the specification asks for its coefficients to be validated on bars they were not fitted on; this score is one minus the squared error of the instrument moves the rolling regression predicts from the driver moves over the squared size of the actual instrument moves on those held-out bars, so a value at or below zero says the sensitivities under every scenario row explain nothing out of sample.
metrics.baseline: The forecast of no instrument move on the same held-out bars

metrics.why: Scenario analysis recommends no decision, so the registry's gap between the utility a solver expected and the utility its decisions earned applies here only as the profit and loss the table promised for a scenario against the profit and loss the book actually made when driver moves like that scenario later occurred; a large gap means the estimated sensitivities broke down when they were needed, and it grades the repricing and not a recommended decision.
metrics.baseline: A gap of zero, where the estimated sensitivities repriced the book correctly

metrics.why: Reading down the table, the shortfall of the current book from the best available positioning under each named scenario shows which story the book is most exposed to and by how much.
metrics.baseline: Zero shortfall, shown under a scenario where the current book is already the best positioning

metrics.why: The shock sizes are opinions, so the ordering of scenarios from most to least damaging should survive scaling each driver shock up or down a little; if it does not, the table's worst case is an artefact of one chosen magnitude.
metrics.baseline: The ordering of scenarios under the shock sizes as written

metrics.why: The sensitivities are re-estimated on a rolling window, and a sensitivity that changes sign from one window to the next cannot support a scenario row built on it.
metrics.baseline: The sensitivities estimated on the previous window

notApplicable.name: Realized Sharpe Ratio
notApplicable.why: The scenario table is a what-if revaluation that trades nothing, so there is no realised return stream to form the ratio.

notApplicable.name: Annualized Alpha
notApplicable.why: No return is earned over time by revaluing a book under a story, and the registry carries no alpha metric.

notApplicable.name: Maximum Drawdown
notApplicable.why: A scenario row is one conditional loss, not an equity path from which a peak-to-trough fall could be measured.

notApplicable.name: Portfolio Turnover
notApplicable.why: Positions are held fixed while the shocks are applied, so the method generates no trades.

notApplicable.name: Calmar Ratio
notApplicable.why: Return over drawdown belongs to a traded account and the native output is a table of conditional outcomes.

notApplicable.name: CVaR (99% Tail Risk)
notApplicable.why: The method assigns no probabilities to its few named scenarios, so there is no loss distribution whose tail could be averaged.

notApplicable.name: Logarithmic loss
notApplicable.why: The specification states that no scenario is forecast to occur, so natively there is no probability for a probability score to grade.

notApplicable.name: Held-out log-likelihood
notApplicable.why: Authored scenarios are a few named stories and not a probability density over outcomes; a density appears only in the runnable stand-in.

asRun.standInNote: The specification applies hand-written driver shocks to a book and tabulates the conditional profit and loss. The runnable adapter instead discovers its scenarios as the components of a Gaussian mixture on the training bars' leading principal components, with the count chosen by the Bayesian information criterion, and records for each a driver table and an outcome table. The as-run numbers measure how well the present bar's resemblance to those historical scenarios, weighted by each scenario's smoothed training up share and passed through a validation-fitted logistic curve, calls direction.
asRun.probabilityNote: The bar's membership weights across the mixture's scenarios are multiplied by each scenario's training up share, shrunk toward the training base rate by readout_prior_strength pseudo-bars, the sum is converted to log-odds, and a two-parameter logistic curve fitted on validation bars gives the probability of up.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per scored bar, one value for the single fit, on the training bars for the scenario-weighted up share before any curve and on the validation bars for the probability after the curve fitted on those same validation bars

meaningful.why: It tests whether bars that resemble scenarios with a high training up share really rise more often than bars that resemble scenarios with a low one; with only a handful of scenarios the scores cluster on a few levels, so read it as a coarse ranking.

The search over the most scenarios the information criterion may choose, the covariance structure, the covariance regularisation and the readout prior strength is scored on inner blocks of the training span by the shared tuning objective, an optimistic selection score and not a result.

The best setting's search score minus the same quantity on the fold's test walk shows how much of the chosen scenario mixture looked good by selection and not by its scenarios differing in what followed them.

It grades the scenario-weighted up share after the validation curve has reshaped it; because the curve is fitted to outcomes the usual objection to scoring raw frequencies does not apply, and the number scores the mixture readout plus that curve.
A bounded reading of the same curve-adjusted scenario mixture, steady even when every scenario's up share sits close to the base rate.
It shows whether the mapping from scenario-weighted up share to realised up share, learned by the curve on validation bars, still holds on test bars; expect few occupied bins.
If the scenarios the mixture found differ in volatility or trend but not in what follows, every bar reads near the base rate and this spread is close to zero.

It counts the hard calls from cutting the curve-adjusted scenario mixture at one half; since the scenario up shares are shrunk toward the base rate, the curve's intercept decides much of which side a bar lands on.
Averaging the hit rate on rising and falling bars shows whether scenario membership separates them or all bars were called the majority way.
One symmetric number for the scenario-based calls, which sits at zero when every bar is assigned the same direction regardless of its scenario weights.
It is what was earned after costs by going long when the curve-adjusted scenario mixture was at least one half and short otherwise, under the engine's rule.
It relates the per-bar profit of the scenario-based call to its variability; zero is an arithmetic marker and not a no-skill level because random calls still pay costs.
It shows the worst losing run of the scenario call, which is where a test period dominated by a scenario whose training up share was misleading would appear.
It sets money won against money lost on the trades opened when the scenario-weighted call changed side, after costs; scenario weights move slowly, so the trade count can be small.
It is the share of closed trades of the scenario call that made money; a trade lasts until the dominant scenarios change the call or the fold ends.

The forecast is the membership-weighted sum of each scenario's shrunk mean scaled move, so this tests whether the historical scenarios differ in the size and sign of what followed them, with no curve involved.
It gives the typical miss in points of the scenario-mean forecast; scenario means are small beside single moves, so this number stays near the no-change error.
It checks the sign of the scenario-weighted mean move directly; with few scenarios many bars round to a zero forecast at the tick, so the denominator shown beside it matters.

The call is the curve applied to scenario up shares while the forecast is the scenario mean move; a share below one shows how often a scenario's typical direction and its average move point opposite ways or the curve shifted the call.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The single training value is the logarithmic loss of the uncalibrated scenario up shares on the bars that produced them, and the validation value comes after a curve fitted on validation bars, so the difference mixes two differently built quantities.
With long_only off and no stop or target the engine is always long or short once it has traded, so this share describes the engine's rule and not the scenario mixture.

caveats: The scenarios are found from the fold's training bars by a Gaussian mixture and are not hand-written stories, so no scenario here describes a shock that has not already happened in that span.

The mixture is fitted without labels and its scenario count is picked by the Bayesian information criterion on training bars; direction enters only through each scenario's smoothed up share and the validation curve.
The per-scenario outcome table of move percentiles and the driver table are written to the log only and are not scored by any metric.
The logistic curve's slope and intercept are fitted on the fold's validation bars, so the validation loss is partly in-sample and only the test walk is out of sample.
The price forecast comes from a second instance of the same mixture whose readout is each scenario's shrunk mean scaled move.

Horizons of consecutive bars overlap, so intervals on these scores need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance; for roots other than MNQ the costs are the MNQ account figures, and the last bar of each fold exits at its close.
